intervals.note: A10: an interval with `start: null` and `end: null` covers no date at all (A3: "start: null covers only [lo(end), hi(end)]"), so the derived state at the build date was `unrecorded`, not `active`, though the laboratory is clearly operating today ("Currently 1300 scientists from 30 different Countries are taking part in the experimental activities of LNGS", src:lngs-overview). No official LNGS or INFN page reached in this session states a foundation, construction or opening date (lngs.infn.it/en/lab-history returned HTTP 404; lngs.infn.it/en gives no date). As a fallback, `start` is set to 1987 on Wikipedia's authority ("the research center became fully operational in 1987") — a rank-12 source, flagged for review — rather than left null, which would misrepresent the laboratory as not currently operating.
intervals.quote: the research center became fully operational in 1987

name: Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso
notes: LNGS is owned in this wave by the fermilab-neutrino-other lead only because ICARUS ran in Hall B; the record covers the laboratory at the level needed for that placement, not the full LNGS programme.
The commonly quoted 3800 m.w.e. overburden is NOT recorded: no page fetched in this session states a metres-water-equivalent figure, only the 1400 m rock thickness.

The foundation/construction dates of LNGS were not found on an official page fetched in this session; the operating interval's start (1987) is sourced to Wikipedia only (src:lngs-wikipedia-history) and is flagged for review.

operator.quote: LNGS is funded by the National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN), the Italian Institution in charge to coordinate and support research in elementary particles physics

depth.note: Stated as an average rock coverage; the mountain profile is asymmetric. No m.w.e. figure is given on the pages fetched.
depth.quote: The 1400 metre-rock thickness above the Laboratory represents a natural coverage that provides a cosmic ray flux reduction by one million times

summary.plain: The largest underground research laboratory in the world, built beside a motorway tunnel under the Gran Sasso mountain in central Italy. About 1400 metres of rock overhead cut the shower of cosmic particles by a factor of a million, which lets very quiet experiments run there.
summary.technical: INFN national laboratory at Assergi (L'Aquila), Italy, with three underground halls of roughly 100 × 20 × 18 m under about 1400 m of rock, hosting low-background neutrino, dark matter and double-beta-decay experiments; the ICARUS T600 ran in Hall B from 2010 to 2013.
